goalInOwnWords: Build a little factory line that turns junk into things worth more money, and make more money than the foreman Sal over six shifts, hitting each shift's money target to earn stars.
stoppedWhere: The results screen after finishing today's yard (shift 6 of 6): 1 star out of 3, $11,151, 'Sal beat you by $1,653', with the 'Try again from shift 4' button showing. I opened the feedback form from there. (Earlier I finished the lesson with all 3 stars and $724.)
stoppedWhy: My break was nearly over, I had finished the whole yard, and the only thing left to chase was $1,653 behind a pretend foreman. Trying again from shift 4 means three more rounds of tapping lit squares for another go at the $11 I missed. I would think about it tomorrow, not right now. Ten minutes for one game is long next to the Mini.

stuck.where: Today's yard, shift 2: after the lit squares ran out, Sal said 'Tap the Shipping Dock on the shelf, then where you think it pays.'
stuck.what: A leftover Dock was on the shelf with no lit square and no 'Show me where'. I could not work out where it should go, or whether I had to place it at all.
stuck.gotOutHow: Dropped it in a random empty square. The forecast did not change, and after the shift the yard labelled it 'nothing came'.

stuck.where: Today's yard, shift 3: the Tuner card, placed without the helper
stuck.what: Where a Tuner should go so that it helps. The 'This shift will pay' line was the same before and after I placed it, so I could not tell if I had done well.
stuck.gotOutHow: Guessed (next to the hopper). Only after the shift did the game say the crusher was the slow one and a Tuner touching it would clear it.

stuck.where: Today's yard, shift 4: '$11 short of the order'
stuck.what: How to find $11 with the parts I had. Moving the Tuner onto the slow crusher only moved the problem to the hopper ('the Crusher waits for scrap') and the forecast stayed the same.
stuck.gotOutHow: I did not. I started the shift and missed the order by $11.

stuck.where: Today's yard, shifts 5 and 6: orders of $3,200 and $4,600
stuck.what: After the missed order the forecast said I was $866 and then $2,266 short before I placed anything, and nothing on screen showed how to catch up.
stuck.gotOutHow: Followed the lit squares and pressed go to finish the game.

confused: The first screen has a lot of cards and numbers: 'Fill six orders', a row of six dollar amounts, stars at 2/4/6 orders. I skimmed it.
'Lit spots: when you ask' on the job card: no idea what it was, so I left it alone.
Two loose machines sit in the yard from the very first screen and nobody says what they are.
In lesson shift 3 the first two machines went red and a 'held you back' label appeared on the furnace, and nothing said whether red was bad.
'38 sped up' and '40 sped up' labels under the Tuner.
Why a card brings a spare Dock I cannot use (shift 2), and the wording 'where you think it pays'.
Plate Press and 'Furnace + Splitter + Dock' with 'No easy spot yet': what a Splitter is, and whether 'no easy spot' means do not take it.
The Tuner panel says 'Sends to the left' when a Tuner does not seem to send anything.
'The lit spots are his game: beat him by finding better': no idea how to find better, the hint only came on the last screen.
A belt piece with two arrows (x2, x4) turning up on the shelf after a machine replaced a belt piece.
annoyed: The lit squares play the game for you. After the lesson I mostly tapped what was lit, so it felt hand-held rather than puzzling.
The advice about what was slow only arrives after the shift. When I placed the Tuner myself nothing warned me.
Missing one order means prices do not rise, so every later order was out of reach. Shifts 5 and 6 were pointless.
'Show me where' is cut off at the right edge of my phone screen, and 'Buy a belt: $20' is half hidden behind the 'This shift will pay' line.
After I scrolled the panel once, the next pick screen stayed scrolled and Sal's bubble and the Show me where button were half cut off.
I did not know I could retry a shift until the very end ('Try again from shift 4'), when I would have used it right after missing by $11.
Too many words on the first screen and on the job card.
A whole game is about ten minutes, long next to the Mini.
pleased: The lesson: one instruction at a time, tap and tap and a payoff. I understood scrap, shards and ingots without reading anything long ('Better goods pay more').
'This shift will pay $X (up $Y)' before I start: I can see my change work.
The yellow 'ORDER FILLED! Every price up 25%' banner sliding across the yard.
Sal as a named rival with lines like 'You're $195 behind Sal', and 'Try again from shift 4' pointing at the exact shift I missed.
The yard labels 'nothing came' and 'held you back' and the 'What held you back' explanation, once I read it.
'Next shift: ...' showing which cards are coming.
The rank line 'Scrap Picker, 1 more star to Yard Hand'.
The survey really took about a minute and nothing on it was cut off.
bestMoment: Lesson shift 3: putting the furnace in, watching the forecast jump from $111 to $576 and gold bars slide down the belt. It was the first time I felt I had built something. A close second was the 'ORDER FILLED' banner on shift 1 of the real yard.
worstMoment: Shift 4's result, 'Missed the order by $11', then finding out the next two orders were out of reach, so the last two shifts were just tapping lit squares and waiting.
oneChange: Make the near miss the game: when I am $11 short, tell me what is slow while I am still placing my part (before I run the shift), and let me redo that shift straight away. That was the one time I wanted another go.
